āgataṃ no mitra balaṃ praharadhvamabhītavat ..
evaṃ brūyādraṇe prāpte mayā bhagnāḥ pare iti .. 7 ..
2.30.d:
स्थूलस्य तस्य पुच्छस्थां कृत्वोल्कां विपुलां द्विज ॥
विसृज्यैनं ततस्तीरमुल्कापातं प्रदर्शयेत् ॥ 2 ॥
अनेनैवात्र सारेण बुद्ध्या निश्चित्य यत्नतः ॥
उत्पातानि तथान्यानि दर्शनीयानि पार्थिवैः ॥ 3 ॥
उद्वेजनं तथा कुर्यात्कुहकैर्द्विविधैर्द्विषाम् ॥
संवत्सरानहार्षश्च नाशं ब्रूयुः परस्य च ॥ 4 ॥
जिगीषुः पृथिवी राज्ये तेन चोद्वेजयेत्परान् ॥
देवतानां प्रसादानि कीर्तनीयानि तस्य तु ॥ 5 ॥
स स्वप्नलाभांश्च तथा जिगीषुः प्रतिकीर्तयेत् ॥।
दुःस्वप्नलाभं च तथा परेषामिति निश्चयः ॥ 6 ॥
आगतं नो मित्र बलं प्रहरध्वमभीतवत् ॥
एवं ब्रूयाद्रणे प्राप्ते मया भग्नाः परे इति ॥ 7 ॥
2.30.m:
a large one, should have a great firebrand tied to its tail, O twice-born;
releasing it swiftly, one should display a fall of meteors.
By this very principle, determining it carefully with the intellect,
other omens should likewise be displayed by kings.
Likewise, one should terrify the enemies with various jugglers;
astrologers should declare the destruction of the adversary,
and the one desirous of conquest in the earthly kingdom should terrify the others with that;
the favours of the gods toward him should indeed be proclaimed.
The one desirous of conquest should proclaim his auspicious dreams,
and likewise that the enemies have received nightmares—this is the rule.
'Our allied army has arrived, strike fearlessly!'
Thus he should speak when battle arrives: 'The enemies have been broken by me!'

2.30.s:
kṣveḍāḥ kilakilāśabdaṃ mama śatrurhatastathā ..
devājñābṛṃhito rājā sannaddhaḥ samaraṃ prati ..8..
2.30.d:
क्ष्वेडाः किलकिलाशब्दं मम शत्रुर्हतस्तथा ॥
देवाज्ञाबृंहितो राजा सन्नद्धः समरं प्रति ॥8॥
2.30.m:
Roars, shouts of joy: 'My enemy has been slain!'
[and] 'Empowered by divine command, the king is girded for battle!'

2.30.s:
evaṃ prakārā dvijavarya māyāḥ kāryā narendrairariṣu prahṛṣṭaiḥ ..
māyāhataḥ śatruratha prasahya śakyaḥ sukhaṃ hantumadīnasattvaḥ .. 9 ..
2.149
puṣkara uvāca ..
caturaṅgaṃ balaṃ rājā māyājālena darśayet ..
sahāyārthamanuprāptāndarśayettridivaukasaḥ .. 1 ..
raktavṛṣṭiśca saṃdarśyā pareṣāṃ śivaraṃ prati ..
chinnāni ripuśīrṣāṇi prasādāgreṣu darśayet .. 2 ..
ādhitsatā sandhimahīnasatva kāryaṃ bhavedrāma mahendrajālam ..
vakṣyāmi taccopaniṣatsu tubhyaṃ yogāni cānyāni jayāvahāni .. 3 ..
2.150
puṣkara uvāca ..
sandhiśca vigrahaścaiva vaiguṇyaṃ kathitaṃ budhaiḥ ..
yadāśritya tathaivānyaiḥ ṣāḍguṇyaṃ parikīrtitam ..1..
sandhiśca nigrahaścaiva yānamāsanameva ca ..
dvaidhībhāvaṃ saṃśrayaṃ ca ṣāḍguṇyaṃ parikīrtitam .. 2 ..
2.30.d:
एवं प्रकारा द्विजवर्य मायाः कार्या नरेन्द्रैररिषु प्रहृष्टैः ॥
मायाहतः शत्रुरथ प्रसह्य शक्यः सुखं हन्तुमदीनसत्त्वः ॥ 9 ॥
2.149
पुष्कर उवाच ॥
चतुरङ्गं बलं राजा मायाजालेन दर्शयेत् ॥
सहायार्थमनुप्राप्तान्दर्शयेत्त्रिदिवौकसः ॥ 1 ॥
रक्तवृष्टिश्च संदर्श्या परेषां शिवरं प्रति ॥
छिन्नानि रिपुशीर्षाणि प्रसादाग्रेषु दर्शयेत् ॥ 2 ॥
आधित्सता सन्धिमहीनसत्व कार्यं भवेद्राम महेन्द्रजालम् ॥
वक्ष्यामि तच्चोपनिषत्सु तुभ्यं योगानि चान्यानि जयावहानि ॥ 3 ॥
2.150
पुष्कर उवाच ॥
सन्धिश्च विग्रहश्चैव वैगुण्यं कथितं बुधैः ॥
यदाश्रित्य तथैवान्यैः षाड्गुण्यं परिकीर्तितम् ॥1॥
सन्धिश्च निग्रहश्चैव यानमासनमेव च ॥
द्वैधीभावं संश्रयं च षाड्गुण्यं परिकीर्तितम् ॥ 2 ॥
2.30.m:
Subtle deceptions of such kinds should be employed by kings against enemies with rejoicing, O best of the twice-born;
for an enemy stricken by deceptions, even if of undiminished spirit, can easily be slain by force.
Puṣkara said:
The king should display a fourfold army by magical illusion;
he should display the gods arrived to assist him.
A rain of blood should be displayed over the camp of the enemies;
he should display severed heads of the enemy upon palace roofs.
When wishing to force a treaty, O one of unyielding spirit, the great sorcery should be employed, O Rāma;
and I shall tell you in the secret doctrines about that and other practices bringing victory.
Puṣkara said:
Peace and war are spoken of by the wise as a duality,
upon which basis the sixfold foreign policy is also described by others.
Peace, war, marching, and encamping,
duplicity, and seeking refuge are described as the sixfold policy.

2.30.s:
paṇabandhaḥ smṛtaḥ sandhirapakārastu vigrahaḥ ..
jigīṣoḥ śatruviṣaye yānaṃ yātrā vidhīyate .. 3 ..
vigrahe'pi svake deśe sthitirāsanamucyate ..
balārdhena pramāṇaṃ tu dvaidhībhāvaṃ taducyate .. 4..
udāsīne madhyame vā saṃśrayātsaṃśrayaḥ smṛtaḥ ..
samena sandhiranveṣyo hīnena ca balīyasaḥ .. .. 5 ..
hīnena vigrahaḥ kāryaḥ svayaṃ rājñā balīyasā ..
tatrāpi tasya pārṣṇistu balīyānna samāśrayet .. 6 ..
āsīnaḥ karmavicchedaṃ śaktaḥ kartuṃ ripuryadā ..
aśuddhapārṣṇirbalavāndvaidhībhāvaṃ samāśrayet .. 7 ..
balinā nigṛhītantu yo manyedyena pārthivaḥ ..
saṃśrayastena kartavyo guṇānāmadhamo guṇaḥ ..8..
bahukṣayavyayāyāsaṃ teṣāṃ yānaṃ prakīrtitam ..
bahulābhakarambhaḥ syāttadā rāma samāśrayet .. 9 ..
2.30.d:
पणबन्धः स्मृतः सन्धिरपकारस्तु विग्रहः ॥
जिगीषोः शत्रुविषये यानं यात्रा विधीयते ॥ 3 ॥
विग्रहेऽपि स्वके देशे स्थितिरासनमुच्यते ॥
बलार्धेन प्रमाणं तु द्वैधीभावं तदुच्यते ॥ 4॥
उदासीने मध्यमे वा संश्रयात्संश्रयः स्मृतः ॥
समेन सन्धिरन्वेष्यो हीनेन च बलीयसः ॥ ॥ 5 ॥
हीनेन विग्रहः कार्यः स्वयं राज्ञा बलीयसा ॥
तत्रापि तस्य पार्ष्णिस्तु बलीयान्न समाश्रयेत् ॥ 6 ॥
आसीनः कर्मविच्छेदं शक्तः कर्तुं रिपुर्यदा ॥
अशुद्धपार्ष्णिर्बलवान्द्वैधीभावं समाश्रयेत् ॥ 7 ॥
बलिना निगृहीतन्तु यो मन्येद्येन पार्थिवः ॥
संश्रयस्तेन कर्तव्यो गुणानामधमो गुणः ॥8॥
बहुक्षयव्ययायासं तेषां यानं प्रकीर्तितम् ॥
बहुलाभकरम्भः स्यात्तदा राम समाश्रयेत् ॥ 9 ॥

2.30.m: One who is bereft of all power should then seek refuge.

2.30.s:
evaṃ ca buddhvā nṛpatirguṇānāṃ kāle ca deśe ca tathā vibhāge ..
samāśrayedbhārgavavaṃśamukhyaṃ caitāvaduktaṃ nṛpatestu kāryam .. 11 ...
2.30.d:
एवं च बुद्ध्वा नृपतिर्गुणानां काले च देशे च तथा विभागे ॥
समाश्रयेद्भार्गववंशमुख्यं चैतावदुक्तं नृपतेस्तु कार्यम् ॥ 11 ॥।
2.30.m:
Thus understanding the division of policies according to time and place,
he should employ them, O chief of Bhṛgu's lineage; and this much is declared as the duty of a king.

2.31.s:
2.151
.. rāma uvāca .. ..
ajasraṃ karma me brūhi rājñāṃ rājīvalocana ..
yacca kāryaṃ narendrāṇāṃ tadhā ca prativatsaram .. 1 ..
2.31.d:
2.151
॥ राम उवाच ॥ ॥
अजस्रं कर्म मे ब्रूहि राज्ञां राजीवलोचन ॥
यच्च कार्यं नरेन्द्राणां तधा च प्रतिवत्सरम् ॥ 1 ॥
2.31.m:
Rāma said:
Tell me the daily duty of kings, O lotus-eyed one,
and what must be done by rulers of men year by year.

2.31.s:
.. puṣkara uvāca .. ...
dvimuhūrtāvaśeṣāyāṃ rātrau nidrāṃ tyajennṛpaḥ ..
veṇuvīṇāmṛdaṅgānāṃ paṭahānāṃ ca niḥsvanaiḥ .. 2 ..
2.31.d:
॥ पुष्कर उवाच ॥ ॥।
द्विमुहूर्तावशेषायां रात्रौ निद्रां त्यजेन्नृपः ॥
वेणुवीणामृदङ्गानां पटहानां च निःस्वनैः ॥ 2 ॥
2.31.m:
Puṣkara said:
With two muhūrtas remaining in the night, the king should give up sleep
to the sounds of flutes, vīṇās, mṛdaṅgas, and drums.

2.31.s:
bandināṃ niḥsvanaiścaiva tathā maṅgalavādinām ..
tataḥ paśyenmahīpālo gūḍhāṃśca puruṣānniśi .. 3 ..
2.31.d:
बन्दिनां निःस्वनैश्चैव तथा मङ्गलवादिनाम् ॥
ततः पश्येन्महीपालो गूढांश्च पुरुषान्निशि ॥ 3 ॥
2.31.m:
and by the cries of bards and those who recite auspicious words.
Then in the night, the ruler of the earth should consult secret agents

2.31.s:
vijñāyante na ye loke tadīyā iti kenacit ..
āyavyayasya śravaṇaṃ tataḥ kāryaṃ yathāvidhi .. 4 ..
2.31.d:
विज्ञायन्ते न ये लोके तदीया इति केनचित् ॥
आयव्ययस्य श्रवणं ततः कार्यं यथाविधि ॥ 4 ॥
2.31.m:
whom no one in the world knows to be his.
Then, in accordance with rule, he should hear the account of income and expenditure.

2.31.s:
vegotsargaṃ tataḥ kṛtvā rājā snānagṛhaṃ vrajet..
dattābhyaṅgaḥ pradoṣe tu kalpamutsāditastataḥ ..5..
2.31.d:
वेगोत्सर्गं ततः कृत्वा राजा स्नानगृहं व्रजेत्॥
दत्ताभ्यङ्गः प्रदोषे तु कल्पमुत्सादितस्ततः ॥5॥
2.31.m:
Having then discharged the urges [of nature], the king should go to the bathhouse.
Anointed with oil, rubbed with fragrant powders according to rule,

2.31.s:
snānaṃ kuryāttataḥ paścāddantadhāvanapūrvakam..
sauṣadhairmantrapūtaistu pānīyairvividhaiḥ śubhaiḥ .. 6 ..
2.31.d:
स्नानं कुर्यात्ततः पश्चाद्दन्तधावनपूर्वकम्॥
सौषधैर्मन्त्रपूतैस्तु पानीयैर्विविधैः शुभैः ॥ 6 ॥
2.31.m:
he should then take his bath, preceded by brushing his teeth,
with diverse auspicious waters mixed with medicinal herbs and consecrated by mantras.

2.31.s:
sandhyāmupāsya prayataḥ kṛtajapyaḥ samāhitaḥ ..
agnyāgāraṃ praviśyātha vahnīn paśyetpurodhasā .. 7 ..
2.31.d:
सन्ध्यामुपास्य प्रयतः कृतजप्यः समाहितः ॥
अग्न्यागारं प्रविश्याथ वह्नीन् पश्येत्पुरोधसा ॥ 7 ॥
2.31.m:
Having performed the dawn twilight worship, purified, having recited his prayers, composed,
he should then enter the fire chamber and see the fires

2.31.s:
hutān samyaktataḥ kuryādvāsudevasya cārcanam ..
duḥsvapnaśamanaṃ karma tatra kuryātpurohitaḥ ..8..
2.31.d:
हुतान् सम्यक्ततः कुर्याद्वासुदेवस्य चार्चनम् ॥
दुःस्वप्नशमनं कर्म तत्र कुर्यात्पुरोहितः ॥8॥
2.31.m:
duly offered by the royal priest, and then perform the worship of Vāsudeva.
The royal priest should there perform the rite that calms bad dreams.

2.31.s:
svayaṃ caupasade vahnau pavitrāṃ juhuyānnṛpaḥ ..
tarpayedudakairdevānpitṝnatha yathāvidhi..9..
2.31.d:
स्वयं चौपसदे वह्नौ पवित्रां जुहुयान्नृपः ॥
तर्पयेदुदकैर्देवान्पितॄनथ यथाविधि॥9॥
2.31.m:
And the king himself should offer the sacred blade of grass into the upasada fire.
He should then satisfy the gods and the ancestors with water according to rule.

2.31.s:
dadyāddvijātaye dhenuṃ savatsāṃ ca sakāñcanām.
śaktyā dhanaiḥ pūjayitvā dattāśīḥ satataṃ dvijaiḥ..2.151.10.. .
2.31.d:
दद्याद्द्विजातये धेनुं सवत्सां च सकाञ्चनाम्।
शक्त्या धनैः पूजयित्वा दत्ताशीः सततं द्विजैः॥2.151.10॥ ।
2.31.m:
He should give to a twice-born a milch cow with its calf and with gold,
having honoured [him] with wealth according to his ability, continuously blessed by the twice-born.

2.31.s:
anuliptastataḥ sragvī suvāsāścāpyalaṃkṛtaḥ ..
darpaṇe ca mukhaṃ paśyetsasuvarṇe ca sarpiṣi .. 11 ..
2.31.d:
अनुलिप्तस्ततः स्रग्वी सुवासाश्चाप्यलंकृतः ॥
दर्पणे च मुखं पश्येत्ससुवर्णे च सर्पिषि ॥ 11 ॥
2.31.m:
Then, anointed [with perfumes], wearing a garland, well dressed and adorned,
he should look at his face in a mirror and in clarified butter with gold.

2.31.s:
ājyaṃ prasannaṃ surabhi yadi syādvijayo bhavet .. .
dīyamāne ca durgandhe patite ca bhayaṃ bhavet..12..
2.31.d:
आज्यं प्रसन्नं सुरभि यदि स्याद्विजयो भवेत् ॥ ।
दीयमाने च दुर्गन्धे पतिते च भयं भवेत्॥12॥
2.31.m:
If the ghee is clear and fragrant, there will be victory;
if it gives off a foul smell or is spilled, there will be danger.

2.31.s:
vikṛtaṃ cenmukhaṃ paśyedrājā mṛtyumavāpnuyāt ..
suprabhaṃ ca yadā paśyettadā tasya śubhaṃ bhavet ..13 ..
2.31.d:
विकृतं चेन्मुखं पश्येद्राजा मृत्युमवाप्नुयात् ॥
सुप्रभं च यदा पश्येत्तदा तस्य शुभं भवेत् ॥13 ॥
2.31.m:
If the king sees a distorted face, he will meet with death;
and when he sees [his face] bright and radiant, then good fortune will be his.

2.31.s:
tatastu śṛṇuyādrājā sāṃvatsaramukhodgatam ..
divase tithinakṣatre sarvāśubhavināśanam ..14..
2.31.d:
ततस्तु शृणुयाद्राजा सांवत्सरमुखोद्गतम् ॥
दिवसे तिथिनक्षत्रे सर्वाशुभविनाशनम् ॥14॥
2.31.m:
Then the king should hear from the mouth of the astrologer
the day, lunar day, and lunar mansion that destroy all inauspiciousness.

2.31.s:
bhiṣajāṃ ca vacaḥ kuryāttatastvārogyavardhanam ..
maṅgalālambhanaṃ kṛtvā tataḥ paśyedgurūnnṛpaḥ ..15..
2.31.d:
भिषजां च वचः कुर्यात्ततस्त्वारोग्यवर्धनम् ॥
मङ्गलालम्भनं कृत्वा ततः पश्येद्गुरून्नृपः ॥15॥
2.31.m:
And he should follow the advice of physicians that promotes health.
Having touched auspicious objects, the king should then look upon his elders.

2.31.s:
kṛtvāśīrgurubhiḥ paścādrājā gacchetsamantataḥ ..
tatrasthānbrāhmaṇānpaśyedamātyānmantriṇastathā ..16..
2.31.d:
कृत्वाशीर्गुरुभिः पश्चाद्राजा गच्छेत्समन्ततः ॥
तत्रस्थान्ब्राह्मणान्पश्येदमात्यान्मन्त्रिणस्तथा ॥16॥
2.31.m:
After receiving blessings from the elders, the king should proceed all around.
He should see the brahmins situated there, as well as the executive officers and counsellors,

2.31.s:
prakṛtīśca mahābhāga pratīhāranibodhataḥ ..
tatretihāsaśravaṇaṃ kuryātkiñcidatandritaḥ .. 17 ..
2.31.d:
प्रकृतीश्च महाभाग प्रतीहारनिबोधतः ॥
तत्रेतिहासश्रवणं कुर्यात्किञ्चिदतन्द्रितः ॥ 17 ॥
2.31.m:
and the subjects, O fortunate one, as announced by the doorkeeper.
There he should listen a little to historical narratives, free from indolence.

2.31.s: tataḥ kāryārthināṃ kuryādyathādhīḥ kāryanirṇayam ..18..
2.31.d: ततः कार्यार्थिनां कुर्याद्यथाधीः कार्यनिर्णयम् ॥18॥
2.31.m: Then, according to his intellect, he should make decisions on matters for those who seek redress.

2.31.s:
vyavahārāṃstataḥ paśyetsamo bhūtvārimitrayoḥ ..
tyaktvā sabhāṃ tataḥ kuryānmantraṃ tu saha mantribhiḥ .. 19 ..
2.31.d:
व्यवहारांस्ततः पश्येत्समो भूत्वारिमित्रयोः ॥
त्यक्त्वा सभां ततः कुर्यान्मन्त्रं तु सह मन्त्रिभिः ॥ 19 ॥
2.31.m:
He should then examine legal disputes, being impartial towards enemy and friend.
Leaving the assembly, he should then deliberate on policy with his ministers,

2.31.s:
yatrāsya kaścittaṃ mantraṃ śṛṇuyānna kathañcana..
ekena saha taṃ kuryānna kuryādbahubhiḥ saha .. 2.151.20 ..
2.31.d:
यत्रास्य कश्चित्तं मन्त्रं शृणुयान्न कथञ्चन॥
एकेन सह तं कुर्यान्न कुर्याद्बहुभिः सह ॥ 2.151.20 ॥
2.31.m:
where no one at all may hear his deliberation.
He should deliberate with one; he should not deliberate with many,

2.31.s:
na ca mūrkhairna cānāmaistathā nādhārmikairnṛpaḥ ..
mantraṃ svadhiṣṭhitaṃ kuryādyena rāṣṭraṃ na dhāvati ..21..
2.31.d:
न च मूर्खैर्न चानामैस्तथा नाधार्मिकैर्नृपः ॥
मन्त्रं स्वधिष्ठितं कुर्याद्येन राष्ट्रं न धावति ॥21॥
2.31.m:
nor with fools, nor with unproven men, nor with the unrighteous, O king.
He should make his deliberation firmly established, so that the realm does not waver.

2.31.s:
rājñāṃ vināśamūlastu kathito mantravibhramaḥ ..
nāśaheturbhavenmantraḥ kuprayuktastvamantravat .. 22 ..
2.31.d:
राज्ञां विनाशमूलस्तु कथितो मन्त्रविभ्रमः ॥
नाशहेतुर्भवेन्मन्त्रः कुप्रयुक्तस्त्वमन्त्रवत् ॥ 22 ॥
2.31.m:
The disclosure of counsel is declared to be the root of destruction for kings.
Counsel improperly applied, like an unchanted mantra, becomes a cause of ruin.

2.31.s:
maṃtre suniścite siddhiḥ kathitā pṛthivīkṣitām ..
kriyamāṇāni karmāṇi yasya vetti na kaścana .. 23 ..
2.31.d:
मंत्रे सुनिश्चिते सिद्धिः कथिता पृथिवीक्षिताम् ॥
क्रियमाणानि कर्माणि यस्य वेत्ति न कश्चन ॥ 23 ॥
2.31.m:
When counsel is well settled, success is declared for rulers of the earth.
He whose undertakings being done no one knows,

2.31.s:
kṛtānyeva vijānāti sa rājā pṛthivīpatiḥ ..
pṛthak ca mantribhirmantraṃ kṛtaṃ vai saṃhitaiḥ punaḥ .. 24 ..
2.31.d:
कृतान्येव विजानाति स राजा पृथिवीपतिः ॥
पृथक् च मन्त्रिभिर्मन्त्रं कृतं वै संहितैः पुनः ॥ 24 ॥
2.31.m:
and knows only when they are completed, he is a king, a lord of the earth.
Counsel taken separately with the ministers, and again [with them] assembled,

2.31.s:
vicāryamātmanaḥ sādhu paścāttatra samāśrayet ..
prajñābhimānī nṛpatirna mantrivacane rataḥ .. 25 ..
2.31.d:
विचार्यमात्मनः साधु पश्चात्तत्र समाश्रयेत् ॥
प्रज्ञाभिमानी नृपतिर्न मन्त्रिवचने रतः ॥ 25 ॥
2.31.m:
having been well considered by himself, he should thereafter adopt.
A king who is proud of his own intellect and not devoted to the words of his ministers

2.31.s:
kṣipraṃ vināśamāyāti taḍāgamiva kājalam ..
ākāragūhanai rājño mantrarakṣā parā matā .. 26 ..
2.31.d:
क्षिप्रं विनाशमायाति तडागमिव काजलम् ॥
आकारगूहनै राज्ञो मन्त्ररक्षा परा मता ॥ 26 ॥
2.31.m:
soon meets with destruction, like a pond of dirty water.
Concealment of physical signs is considered the highest protection of counsel for a king.

2.31.s:
ākārairiṅgitaiḥ prājñā mantraṃ jānanti paṇḍitāḥ ..
sāṃvatsarāṇāṃ vaidyānāṃ mantriṇāṃ vacane rataḥ..27..
2.31.d:
आकारैरिङ्गितैः प्राज्ञा मन्त्रं जानन्ति पण्डिताः ॥
सांवत्सराणां वैद्यानां मन्त्रिणां वचने रतः॥27॥
2.31.m:
Wise and learned men discern counsel through physical signs and gestures.
Devoted to the words of astrologers, physicians, and ministers,

2.31.s:
rājā vibhūtimāpnoti ciraṃ yaśasi tiṣṭhati ..
ta enaṃ mṛgayāsaktaṃ dhārayanti vipaścitaḥ..28..
2.31.d:
राजा विभूतिमाप्नोति चिरं यशसि तिष्ठति ॥
त एनं मृगयासक्तं धारयन्ति विपश्चितः॥28॥
2.31.m:
a king attains prosperity and abides long in fame.
Those wise men restrain him when he is addicted to hunting,

2.31.s:
strīṣu māne tathākṣeṣu vṛthā jyāyāṃśca bhārgava ..
karapraṇayane saktaṃ hiṃsāyāṃ ca narādhipam .. 29 ..
2.31.d:
स्त्रीषु माने तथाक्षेषु वृथा ज्यायांश्च भार्गव ॥
करप्रणयने सक्तं हिंसायां च नराधिपम् ॥ 29 ॥
2.31.m:
O Bhārgava, or when he is vainly superior in [his indulgence in] women, pride, and dice,
and they restrain the lord of men when he is addicted to levying unjust taxes and violence,

2.31.s:
tathā parokṣanindāyāṃ balavadvigrahe'pi ca ..
anyeṣu cāpyanartheṣu prasaktaṃ vārayanti tam .. 2.151.30 ..
2.31.d:
तथा परोक्षनिन्दायां बलवद्विग्रहेऽपि च ॥
अन्येषु चाप्यनर्थेषु प्रसक्तं वारयन्ति तम् ॥ 2.151.30 ॥
2.31.m:
as well as backbiting and conflict with the powerful,
and they restrain him when he is attached to other harmful pursuits.

2.31.s:
mantraṃ kṛtvā tataḥ kuryādvyāyāmaṃ pṛthivīpatiḥ ..
rathe nāge tathaivāśve khaḍge dhanuṣi cāpyatha .. 31 ..
2.31.d:
मन्त्रं कृत्वा ततः कुर्याद्व्यायामं पृथिवीपतिः ॥
रथे नागे तथैवाश्वे खड्गे धनुषि चाप्यथ ॥ 31 ॥
2.31.m:
Having deliberated, the lord of the earth should then take exercise
with the chariot, the elephant, the horse, and also with the sword and the bow,

2.31.s:
anyeṣu caiva śastreṣu niyuddheṣu tataḥ param ..
padbhyāmudvartitaḥ snātaḥ paśyedviṣṇuṃ supūjitam..32..
2.31.d:
अन्येषु चैव शस्त्रेषु नियुद्धेषु ततः परम् ॥
पद्भ्यामुद्वर्तितः स्नातः पश्येद्विष्णुं सुपूजितम्॥32॥
2.31.m:
and with other weapons, and thereafter in hand-to-hand combat.
Having been massaged from his feet up and bathed, he should see Viṣṇu duly worshipped.

2.31.s:
hutaṃ ca pāvakaṃ paśyedviprānpaśyetsupūjitān..
svāmino dakṣiṇābhiśca pūjitānbhṛgunandana ..33..
2.31.d:
हुतं च पावकं पश्येद्विप्रान्पश्येत्सुपूजितान्॥
स्वामिनो दक्षिणाभिश्च पूजितान्भृगुनन्दन ॥33॥
2.31.m:
He should see the fire offered into, and he should see the brahmins well honoured,
and honoured with sacrificial fees by their master, O descendant of Bhṛgu.

2.31.s:
tato'nuliptaḥ surabhiḥ sragvī rucirabhūṣaṇaḥ ..
suvāsā bhojanaṃ kuryādgītaṃ ca śṛṇuyāttadā ..34..
2.31.d:
ततोऽनुलिप्तः सुरभिः स्रग्वी रुचिरभूषणः ॥
सुवासा भोजनं कुर्याद्गीतं च शृणुयात्तदा ॥34॥
2.31.m:
Then, anointed, fragrant, garlanded, with splendid ornaments
and fine clothes, he should take his meal and listen then to music.

2.31.s:
āptaṃ parīkṣitaṃ vahnau mṛgapakṣīṅgitaistathā..
pūrvaṃ parīkṣitaṃ cānyairjāṃgulyā cābhimantritam..35..
2.31.d:
आप्तं परीक्षितं वह्नौ मृगपक्षीङ्गितैस्तथा॥
पूर्वं परीक्षितं चान्यैर्जांगुल्या चाभिमन्त्रितम्॥35॥
2.31.m:
[Food that is] trustworthy, tested in fire and by the reactions of beasts and birds,
tested beforehand by others and consecrated with anti-poison charms,

2.31.s:
viṣaghnāṃśca maṇīnrājā dhārayannauṣadhīṃstathā ..
bhuktvā gṛhītatāmbūlaḥ parikramya viśeṣataḥ .. 36..
2.31.d:
विषघ्नांश्च मणीन्राजा धारयन्नौषधींस्तथा ॥
भुक्त्वा गृहीतताम्बूलः परिक्रम्य विशेषतः ॥ 36॥
2.31.m:
while wearing poison-dispelling gems and herbs, the king,
having eaten, taken betel, and walked about particularly,

2.31.s:
śayane vāmapārśvena tataḥ śāstrāṇi cintayet ..
koṣṭhāgārāyudhāgārānprati cāgryaṃ ca vāhanam .. 37 ..
2.31.d:
शयने वामपार्श्वेन ततः शास्त्राणि चिन्तयेत् ॥
कोष्ठागारायुधागारान्प्रति चाग्र्यं च वाहनम् ॥ 37 ॥
2.31.m:
lying on his bed on his left side, should then reflect upon the treatises.
Having inspected the granaries, the armouries, the foremost mounts,

2.31.s:
yodhāṃśca dṛṣṭvā cānvāsyā tataḥ sandhyā ca paścimā ..
kāryāṇi cintayitvā ca preṣayitvā tataścarān ..
antaḥpuracaro bhūtvā laghu bhuktvā tathā hitam .. 38 ..
2.31.d:
योधांश्च दृष्ट्वा चान्वास्या ततः सन्ध्या च पश्चिमा ॥
कार्याणि चिन्तयित्वा च प्रेषयित्वा ततश्चरान् ॥
अन्तःपुरचरो भूत्वा लघु भुक्त्वा तथा हितम् ॥ 38 ॥
2.31.m:
and the warriors, he should then attend the evening twilight worship.
Having reflected on his affairs and then dispatched his spies,
entering the inner apartments and eating lightly and wholesome food,

2.31.s:
saveṇuvīṇāpaṭahasvanena seveta nidrāṃ kṛtapūrvarakṣām ..
etadyaśasyaṃ hi narādhipānāmājasrikaṃ te kathitaṃ vidhānam .. 39 ..
2.152
.. puṣkara uvāca ..
rājā tu janmanakṣatre prati māsaṃ samācaret ..
janmanaḥ kṣālanaṃ karma yattatpūrvaṃ mayeritam .. 1 ..
puṣpasnānaṃ tataḥ kuryātpratimāsaṃ narādhipaḥ ..
saṃkrāntau pūjayetsūryaṃ bālaminduṃ tathaiva ca ..2 ..
grahaṃ sampūjayedrājā nirgataṃ ravimaṇḍalāt..
agastyasyodaye kāryā tathā pūjā narādhipaiḥ .. 3 ..
pūjayeccaturo māsānprasuptaṃ madhusūdanam ..
proṣṭhapādāmale rakṣetpūjayecca śatakratum ..4..
navamyāmāśvayucchukle bhadrakālīṃ ca pūjayet ..
ravau svātimanuprāpte kuryānnīrājanaṃ tathā..5..
2.31.d:
सवेणुवीणापटहस्वनेन सेवेत निद्रां कृतपूर्वरक्षाम् ॥
एतद्यशस्यं हि नराधिपानामाजस्रिकं ते कथितं विधानम् ॥ 39 ॥
2.152
॥ पुष्कर उवाच ॥
राजा तु जन्मनक्षत्रे प्रति मासं समाचरेत् ॥
जन्मनः क्षालनं कर्म यत्तत्पूर्वं मयेरितम् ॥ 1 ॥
पुष्पस्नानं ततः कुर्यात्प्रतिमासं नराधिपः ॥
संक्रान्तौ पूजयेत्सूर्यं बालमिन्दुं तथैव च ॥2 ॥
ग्रहं सम्पूजयेद्राजा निर्गतं रविमण्डलात्॥
अगस्त्यस्योदये कार्या तथा पूजा नराधिपैः ॥ 3 ॥
पूजयेच्चतुरो मासान्प्रसुप्तं मधुसूदनम् ॥
प्रोष्ठपादामले रक्षेत्पूजयेच्च शतक्रतुम् ॥4॥
नवम्यामाश्वयुच्छुक्ले भद्रकालीं च पूजयेत् ॥
रवौ स्वातिमनुप्राप्ते कुर्यान्नीराजनं तथा॥5॥
2.31.m:
to the sound of flutes, lutes, and drums, he should take to sleep, his protection having first been secured.
This daily routine, which brings fame to rulers of men, has thus been told to you.
2.152
Puṣkara said:
On his birth-asterism every month, the king should perform
the rite of cleansing one’s birth, which was previously spoken of by me.
The ruler of men should then perform a flower bath each month.
At a solstice or equinox, he should worship the sun and likewise the crescent moon.
The king should worship a planet that has emerged from the orb of the sun.
Likewise, worship should be performed by rulers of men at the rising of Agastya.
He should worship Madhusūdana while he sleeps for four months.
In the bright half of Proṣṭhapada, he should observe protection and worship Śatakratu.
On the ninth day of the bright half of Āśvayuja, he should worship Bhadrakālī.
When the sun reaches Svātī, he should likewise perform the lustration of arms.

2.31.s:
saṃvatsarātkoṭihomaṃ kuryācca ghṛtakevalam..
rājyasaṃvatsaragranthau kuryāttadrudrapūjanam..
karmāṇyathaitāni narādhipasya nityāni te rāma mayoditāni ..
etāni kṛtvā vidhivannarendraściraṃ samāgrāṃ vasudhāṃ praśāsti..7..
2.153
rāma uvāca ..
kathaṃ hi caturo māsānkāryaṃ keśavapūjanam ..
pārthivena suraśreṣṭha tanmamācakṣva pṛcchataḥ .. 1 ..
puṣkara uvāca ..
udyuktena sadā bhāvyaṃ rājñā bhṛgukulodvaha ..
āṣāḍhaśuklapakṣānte rājā sthānamupāśrayet .. 2 ..
adhṛṣyaṃ pararāṣṭrāṇāṃ prabhūtayavasendhanam ..
toyopetaṃ vipaṅkaṃ ca prāvṛṭkālahataṃ tathā ..3..
yatrasthaśca svaviṣayaṃ sarvaṃ śaknoti rakṣitum ..
tatrasthaścaturo māsānajāṃśca poṣayennṛpaḥ .. 4 ..
snehapānairbahuvidhaiḥ pratipānaiśca bhārgava ..
āṣāḍhaśuklapakṣānte daśamyūrddhvaṃ narādhipaḥ .. 5 ..
2.31.d:
संवत्सरात्कोटिहोमं कुर्याच्च घृतकेवलम्॥
राज्यसंवत्सरग्रन्थौ कुर्यात्तद्रुद्रपूजनम्॥
कर्माण्यथैतानि नराधिपस्य नित्यानि ते राम मयोदितानि ॥
एतानि कृत्वा विधिवन्नरेन्द्रश्चिरं समाग्रां वसुधां प्रशास्ति॥7॥
2.153
राम उवाच ॥
कथं हि चतुरो मासान्कार्यं केशवपूजनम् ॥
पार्थिवेन सुरश्रेष्ठ तन्ममाचक्ष्व पृच्छतः ॥ 1 ॥
पुष्कर उवाच ॥
उद्युक्तेन सदा भाव्यं राज्ञा भृगुकुलोद्वह ॥
आषाढशुक्लपक्षान्ते राजा स्थानमुपाश्रयेत् ॥ 2 ॥
अधृष्यं परराष्ट्राणां प्रभूतयवसेन्धनम् ॥
तोयोपेतं विपङ्कं च प्रावृट्कालहतं तथा ॥3॥
यत्रस्थश्च स्वविषयं सर्वं शक्नोति रक्षितुम् ॥
तत्रस्थश्चतुरो मासानजांश्च पोषयेन्नृपः ॥ 4 ॥
स्नेहपानैर्बहुविधैः प्रतिपानैश्च भार्गव ॥
आषाढशुक्लपक्षान्ते दशम्यूर्द्ध्वं नराधिपः ॥ 5 ॥
2.31.m:
At the turn of a year, he should perform a ten-million oblation offering using ghee alone. / On the anniversary of his royal consecration, he should perform the worship of Rudra. / Now these perpetual duties of the ruler of men have been spoken to you by me, O Rāma; / having performed these according to rule, the king rules the entire earth for a long time.
Rāma said: / How indeed should the worship of Keśava be performed during the four months / by an earthly king, O best of gods? Tell that to me as I ask.
Puṣkara said: / A king must always be prepared, O bearer of the Bhṛgu lineage. / At the end of the bright fortnight of Āṣāḍha, the king should take up a station
that is unassailable by hostile kingdoms, abundant in grass and firewood, / supplied with water, free of mud, and likewise untouched by the [hazards of the] rainy season,
and staying where he is able to protect his entire domain. / Staying there, the king should nourish his subjects for four months
with various kinds of fatty drinks and after-potions, O descendant of Bhṛgu. / At the end of the bright fortnight of Āṣāḍha, after the tenth day, the ruler of men

2.31.s:
utsavantu mahatkuryāddevasya cārcane rataḥ ..
arcāyāṃ vā paṭe vāpi kṛtaṃ devamathārcayeta .. 6 ..
devabhogamayaṃ viṣṇuṃ śrīsahāyamarindamam ..
balibhirvividhābhistu puṣpairdhūpaiḥ sugandhibhiḥ .. 7 ..
utsavaṃ tu mahatkuryāttataḥ pañcadinaṃ nṛpaḥ ..
tataḥ prabhṛti nityaṃ syādvāsudevasya pūjanam ..8..
sāttvatairbhārgavaśreṣṭha sāṃvatsarapurohitaiḥ ..
gītanṛtyaistathā devaṃ viśeṣeṇātra pūjayet ..9..
asminneva tathā kāle koṭihomaṃ samācaret ..
kārtikyāṃ tatsamāptistu yathā bhavati bhārgava..2.153.10..
śuklapakṣatribhāgentye kārtikasya tato nṛpaḥ ..
utsavaṃ sumahatkuryāddevadevārcanaṃ tathā .. 11 ..
vaikuṇṭhaṃ pūjayeddevamarcāyāmathavā paṭe ..
mahādānaṃ tato dadyātprekṣyāṃ dadyāttathaiva ca .. 12 ..
2.31.d:
उत्सवन्तु महत्कुर्याद्देवस्य चार्चने रतः ॥
अर्चायां वा पटे वापि कृतं देवमथार्चयेत ॥ 6 ॥
देवभोगमयं विष्णुं श्रीसहायमरिन्दमम् ॥
बलिभिर्विविधाभिस्तु पुष्पैर्धूपैः सुगन्धिभिः ॥ 7 ॥

2.31.m:
should hold a great festival, intent on worshipping the deity. / He should then worship the god fashioned in an image or on a cloth,
Viṣṇu, full of divine delights, accompanied by Śrī, the slayer of his foes, / with various offerings, flowers, and fragrant incenses.
The king should hold a great festival for five days thereafter; / from that time onward, there should be daily worship of Vāsudeva.
O best of the Bhṛgus, through the Sāttvatas, astrologers, and royal priests, / he should especially worship the god here with songs and dances.
At this very time he should likewise perform a ten-million oblation offering, / so that its conclusion occurs on the full-moon day of Kārtika, O descendant of Bhṛgu.
Then, in the final third of the bright fortnight of Kārtika, the king / should hold a very great festival as well as the worship of the God of gods.
He should worship the god Vaikuṇṭha in an image or on a cloth; / then he should give a great gift and likewise present a theatrical performance,

2.31.m:
of wrestlers, acrobats, and actors together with dancers; / the lord of the earth should thus make all preparations for the expedition.
Having done this, an expedition is to be undertaken by kings / in the autumn season, free from anxieties, with well-nourished horses, chariots, and elephants.
And thus for four months the supreme god, the remover [of sins], is to be worshipped by the king; / and having worshipped Madhusūdana whose insignia have been laid aside, the expedition shall bestow desired success.
Rāma said: / How should the worship of Śakra be performed by a king, O best of gods, / properly in the month of Bhādrapada? Tell that to me as I ask.
Puṣkara said: / Formerly the gods, broken in battle by the asuras, O foremost of the Bhṛgus, / went for refuge to Brahmā, who is intent on the welfare of all beings.
To those gods, all bewildered, conquered by the Dānavas and facing slaughter, / Brahmā then spoke, [directing them] to Madhusūdana in the Ocean of Milk:
'Go all together; he will bring about your welfare.' / Having spoken thus, all the gods went to Keśava in the Ocean of Milk,

2.31.m:
and then they beheld the god Vāsudeva, the teacher of the world, / resembling a cloud swollen with nectar, bearing the conch, discus, and mace.
And the thirty [gods] praised that fortunate one again and again, / the god who is the lord of all, the sole cause of the world.
The gods said: / Homage to you, O lotus-eyed one, loving toward those who come for refuge, / destroyer of the pride of the hosts of the gods' enemies, giver of happiness to the king of the thirty [gods]!
O you whose garment resembles gold, whose excellent banner bears Tārkṣya, / who sleep upon the couch of Śeṣa, darling of Lakṣmī's heart!
O you whose lotus feet are rubbed by the crest-jewels of gods and asuras, / whose lotus hands are adorned with wide-open, beautiful lotuses!
And when we were once broken by the asuras, you / were our refuge; therefore, routed by the Daityas, we have come into your presence.
Be gracious, O Lord of the gods of gods! Slay those vilest of asuras, / who continually afflict us, O Lord of the gods of gods!
The Lord said: / I will give you this banner, which destroys enemies, / by the mere sight of which the Dānavas will flee here.

श्रीपुष्कर उवाच ॥
एवमुक्त्वा ध्वजं तेषां ददौ विष्णुरनुत्तमम् ॥
सौवर्णमुच्छ्रितं दिव्यं शक्रध्वजमिति श्रुतम् ॥13॥
तमादाय सुराः सर्वे प्रययुर्दानवालयम्॥

तत्तेजसा महाभाग मूर्च्छीभूताः क्षणेन तु ॥
मूर्च्छितास्तु ततो दैत्यास्त्रिदशैर्विनिपातिताः ॥16 ॥
केचिद्भग्ना दिशो जग्मुस्समुद्रं विविशुस्ततः ॥
ततो लब्धजयः शक्रः पूजयामास तं ध्वजम् ॥ 17॥
पूजयित्वा नृपतये वसवे प्रददौ तदा ॥
गर्गोक्तेन विधानेन तं च पूजितवान्वसुः ॥ 18॥
तेनास्य तुष्टो मघवानिदं वचनमब्रवीत् ॥
इन्द्र उवाच ॥
येप्यन्ये भूमिपाः श्रेष्ठाः शक्रध्वजमहोत्सवम् ॥19॥
2.31.m:
Illustrious Puṣkara said: / Having spoken thus, Viṣṇu gave them the peerless banner, / golden, raised high, divine, renowned as Śakra's banner.
Taking it, all the gods set out for the abode of the Dānavas. / Hearing that the gods had arrived, the Dānavas then came forth,
all with their forces well equipped and with weapons raised. / And seeing the army of the gods radiant with Śakra's banner,
they were instantly stupefied by its splendor, O fortunate one; / and being stupefied, the Daityas were then struck down by the thirty [gods].
Some, broken, fled to the directions; others entered the ocean. / Thereupon Śakra, having attained victory, worshipped that banner.
Having worshipped it, he then presented it to King Vasu; / and Vasu worshipped it according to the rule declared by Garga.
Pleased with him on account of this, Maghavan spoke these words. / Indra said: / Whatever other excellent kings [celebrate] the great festival of Śakra's banner

2.31.m:
from this day forward, O knower of dharma, attentively performing it, / for them there will always be manifold prosperity, O twice-born.
Famine, pestilence, disease, and fear of an enemy army— / all these perish when the festival of Śakra's banner is performed.
Puṣkara said: / From that time onward, kings, O Rāma, perform the great festival of Śakra / as declared by Garga, which destroys all fear.
Auspicious, bringing renown, destroying enemies, granting fame, and bestowing the fruits of dharma, / the festival of Śakra must be performed diligently by kings for victory; I shall describe that to you.
2.155
Puṣkara said: / In the eastern quarter of the camp, on an auspicious plot of ground / that slopes towards the east or north, an auspicious pavilion should be made for Śakra,
with garments, clean beds, and various dyes as well. / Then, having set up the place for Śakra's banner in the middle with care,
one should make an image on cloth of Maghavat on its right side.

तस्याः प्रवेशे नगरं पताकाध्वजमालि च ॥ 11 ॥
2.31.m:
On the left side, on a cloth, one should likewise depict goddess Śacī. / In the bright fortnight of the month of Proṣṭhapada, starting from the first lunar day in due order,
worship of the two must constantly be performed by rulers of the earth. / Then, O king, according to the rite for entering the forest, [bringing] Śakra's pole,
one should bring it by means of an ox-cart, or else by swift men. / It should be made of arjuna, ajakarṇa, priyaka, or vaca,
or likewise of suradāru, or of udumbara, / or of candana, O Rāma, or of padmaka.
If none of these woods is available, one should make a bamboo pole / bound with gold, O knower of dharma, and bring it properly inside.
On the eighth day of the bright fortnight of Proṣṭhapada, O slayer of foes, / Śakra's pole is to be known as being of standard measure, O king.
Reduced by four aṅgulas at the top, it brings welfare; / having cut eight [aṅgulas] off at the base, he should cast it into water.
Having raised it up, he should enter the city; it proceeds in proper order. / At its entry, the city should be decorated with strings of flags and banners,

सिक्तराजपथं कुर्यात्तथालंकृतबालकम् ॥
नटनर्तकसङ्कीर्णं तथा पूजितदैवतम् ॥ 12 ॥
सम्पूजितगृहं राम तथा पूजितवानयम् ॥
पौरैरनुगतो राजा सुवंशैः फलपाणिभिः ॥13॥
अष्टम्यां वाद्यघोषेण तां तु यष्टिं प्रवेशयेत् ॥
प्राक्छिरास्तां ततः कुर्याद्वस्त्रैः संच्छादितां शुभैः ॥ 14 ॥
पूजितां पूजयेत्तान्तु यावत्सा द्वादशीफलम् ॥
एकादश्यां सोपवासो नृपः कुर्यात्प्रजागरम् ॥ 15 ॥
सांवत्सरेण सहितो मन्त्रिणा सपुरोधसा ॥
रात्रौ जागरणं कार्यं नागरेण जनेन तु ॥ 16 ॥
स्थानेस्थाने महाभाग देया प्रेक्ष्या तथा मधु ॥
पूजयेन्नृत्यगीतेन रात्रौ शक्रं नराधिपः ॥ 17 ॥
द्वादश्यां तु शिरःस्नातो नृपतिः प्रयतस्ततः ॥
यन्त्रेणोत्थापनं कुर्याच्छक्रकेतोः समाहितः ॥ 18 ॥
2.31.m:
its royal highway sprinkled, with children adorned, / crowded with actors and dancers, and with deities worshipped.
With houses properly worshipped, O Rāma, and with sacred trees worshipped, / the king should be followed by citizens of good families bearing fruits in their hands.
On the eighth day, to the sound of musical instruments, he should bring that pole in; / then he should set it with its tip to the east, covered with auspicious garments.
He should worship it, already revered, until that reward of the twelfth day. / On the eleventh day, fasting, the king should keep vigil,
accompanied by the astrologer, the minister, and the royal chaplain; / and a night vigil should be kept by the city people.
In various places, O fortunate one, spectacles and wine should be given; / the king should worship Śakra at night with dance and song.
On the twelfth day, having bathed his head, the king, purified and collected in mind, / should raise Śakra's banner by means of a mechanical apparatus.

2.31.d:
सुयंत्रितं तु तं कुर्याद्गृहं स्तम्भचतुष्टयम् ॥
पूजयेत्तन्महाभाग गन्धमाल्यान्नसम्पदा ॥ 19 ॥
नित्यं च पटयोः पूजा यष्टिपूजां च कारयेत् ॥
बलिभिस्तु विचित्राभिस्तथा ब्राह्मणपूजनैः ॥2.155.20॥
नित्यं च जुहुयान्मन्त्रान्पुरोधाः शाक्रवैष्णवान् ॥
नित्यं नृत्येन गीतेन तथा शक्रं च पूजयेत् ॥ 21 ॥
द्वादश्यां पूजयेद्राजा ब्राह्मणान्धनसञ्चयैः ॥
विशेषेण च धर्मज्ञ सांवत्सर पुरोहितौ ॥ 22 ॥
उत्थाने च प्रवेशे च शक्रभूयान्नराधिपः ॥
वक्ष्यमाणेन मन्त्रेण कालवित्सपुरोहितः ॥ 23 ॥
पूजयेदुत्थितं केतुं भूषणैर्विविधैरपि ॥
छत्रेण च तथा वस्त्रैर्माल्यदामैस्तथैव च ॥ 24 ॥
एवं सम्पूजयेद्राम तदा दिनचतुष्टयम् ॥
पञ्चमे दिवसे प्राप्ते शुक्रकेतुं विसर्जयेत् ॥ 25॥
2.31.m:
He should secure it well within a pavilion of four pillars; / he should worship it, O fortunate one, with an abundance of perfumes, garlands, and food.
He should daily perform the worship of the two cloth images and the worship of the pole, / with various oblations and with worship of brahmins.
The royal chaplain should daily offer oblations with mantras to Śakra and Viṣṇu; / and he should daily worship Śakra with dance and song.
On the twelfth day, the king should honor the brahmins with heaps of wealth, / and especially the astrologer and the royal chaplain, O knower of dharma.
At its raising and at its entry, the king should embody Śakra / through the mantra to be spoken, accompanied by the royal chaplain who knows the right time.
He should worship the raised banner with various ornaments, / with a parasol, with garments, and with garlands and wreaths.
In this way, O Rāma, he should worship it for four days; / when the fifth day arrives, he should dismiss Śakra's banner.

पूजयित्वा महाभाग बलेन चतुरङ्गिणा ॥
नीत्वा करीन्द्रैस्त्रितयं ततो नद्यां प्रवाहयेत् ॥ 26 ॥
वाद्यघोषेण महता संगीतं तत्र कीर्तितम् ॥
पौरा जानपदास्तत्र क्रीडां कुर्युस्तदाम्भसि ॥
उत्सवं च तथा कार्यं जलतीरगतैर्महत् ॥ 27 ॥

नाशं तथा शत्रुगणस्य राम महत्प्रसादं त्रिदशाधिनाथम् ॥ 28 ॥
2.31.m:
Having worshipped it, O fortunate one, [accompanied] by the fourfold army, / having it carried by lordly elephants, he should then set the triad afloat in a river.
With a great sound of musical instruments, music is celebrated there; / the urban and rural folk should make sport in the water then, / and a great festival should be held by those assembled on the riverbank.
Having performed this rite, the king attains an increase of wealth and vehicles, / the destruction of hosts of enemies, O Rāma, and the great grace of the lord of the gods.

2.157
राम उवाच ॥
शक्रोच्छ्राये तु यान्मन्त्रान्सोपवासो नृपः पठेत् ॥
तानहं श्रोतुमिच्छामि सर्वधर्मभृतां वर ॥1॥
पुष्कर उवाच ॥
शृणु मन्त्रानिमान्सम्यक्सर्वकिल्बिषनाशनान् ॥
प्राप्ते शक्रध्वजोच्छ्राये यः पठेत्प्रयतो नृपः ॥2॥
वरस्त्विन्द्रजिता मित्रवृत्रहन्पाकशासन ॥
देवदेव महाभाग त्वं हि वर्धिष्णुतां गतः॥3॥
त्वं प्रभुः शाश्वतश्चैव सर्वभूतहिते रतः॥
अनन्ततेजो विरजो यशोविजयवर्धनः ॥
अप्रभुस्त्वं प्रभुर्नित्यमुत्तिष्ठ सुरपूजित ॥ 4 ॥
ब्रह्मा स्वयंभूर्भगवान्सर्वलोकपितामहः ॥
रुद्रः पिनाकभृद्दृप्तश्चतसृद्वयसंस्तुतः ॥ 5 ॥
2.32.m:
And cows accompanied by gold, garments, and silver must be given to foremost twice-born men; / when this is done, evil is pacified, and the ruler of men prospers.
Rāma said:
Now, what mantras should a king recite, while fasting, during the raising of Śakra['s banner]?
I wish to hear those, O best of all upholders of dharma.
Puṣkara said:
Hear completely these mantras that destroy all sins,
which a restrained king should recite when the time for raising Śakra's banner arrives:
"O best one, conqueror of Indra['s foes], friend, slayer of Vṛtra, chastiser of Pāka,
O god of gods, fortunate one, you have indeed attained growth.
You are the lord, eternal, devoted to the welfare of all beings,
of infinite splendour, free of passion, increasing fame and victory.
Though sovereign, you are always the lord; arise, O you who are worshipped by the gods!
May the self-born god Brahmā, the grandfather of all the worlds,
[and] Rudra, wielder of the Pināka, proud, praised by the two pairs [of Vedas],

2.32.m:
and the guide and maker of Yoga, Viṣṇu of wide strides—
may these mighty ones constantly increase your splendour!
May the god Brahmā, without beginning or end, the eternal creator,
and Agni, made of splendour, and the portion who is Rudra's essence, the son of Pārvatī,
Kārtikeya, bearer of the spear, six-faced, and holder of the mace,
the hundredfold, the choice, the granter of boons, the omnipresent lord, increase [your] splendour!
May the god, the commander of the army, Skanda, worshipped by the foremost of the gods,
the Ādityas, the Vasus, the Rudras, the Sādhyas, the gods, and the two Aśvins,

2.32.s:
bhṛguraṅgirasaścaiva viśvedevā marudgaṇāḥ ..
lokapālāstrayaścaiva candraḥ sūryo'nalo'nilaḥ .. 2.157.10 ..
2.32.d:
भृगुरङ्गिरसश्चैव विश्वेदेवा मरुद्गणाः ॥
लोकपालास्त्रयश्चैव चन्द्रः सूर्योऽनलोऽनिलः ॥ 2.157.10 ॥
2.32.m:
Bhṛgu and the Aṅgirases, the Viśvedevas, the hosts of Maruts,
the three world-protectors, the Moon, the Sun, Fire, and Wind,

2.32.s:
devāśca ṛṣayaścaiva yakṣagandharvarākṣasāḥ ..
samudrā girayaścaiva nadyo bhūtāni yāni ca .. 11 ..
2.32.d:
देवाश्च ऋषयश्चैव यक्षगन्धर्वराक्षसाः ॥
समुद्रा गिरयश्चैव नद्यो भूतानि यानि च ॥ 11 ॥
2.32.m:
and the gods, the sages, the yakṣas, gandharvas, and rākṣasas,
the oceans, the mountains, the rivers, and whatever beings [there are],

2.32.s:
tejastapāṃsi satyaṃ ca lakṣmīḥ śrīḥ kīrtireva ca ..
pravardhayatu tattejo jaya śakra śacīpate..12..
2.32.d:
तेजस्तपांसि सत्यं च लक्ष्मीः श्रीः कीर्तिरेव च ॥
प्रवर्धयतु तत्तेजो जय शक्र शचीपते॥12॥
2.32.m:
splendour, austerities, truth, Lakṣmī, Śrī, and fame—
may [all these] increase that splendour of yours! Victory, O Śakra, O husband of Śacī!

2.32.s:
tava cāpi jayānnityaṃ tviha saṃpadyate śubham ..
prasīda rājñāṃ viprāṇāṃ prajānāmapi sarvaśaḥ .. 13 ..
2.32.d:
तव चापि जयान्नित्यं त्विह संपद्यते शुभम् ॥
प्रसीद राज्ञां विप्राणां प्रजानामपि सर्वशः ॥ 13 ॥
2.32.m:
And always from your victory good fortune arises here [on earth].
Be gracious to the kings, to the brahmins, and to the subjects everywhere!

2.32.s:
tava prasādātpṛthivī nityaṃ sasyavatī bhavet ..
śivaṃ bhavatu nirvighnaṃ śamyaṃtāmītayo bhṛśam ..14 ..
2.32.d:
तव प्रसादात्पृथिवी नित्यं सस्यवती भवेत् ॥
शिवं भवतु निर्विघ्नं शम्यंतामीतयो भृशम् ॥14 ॥
2.32.m:
By your favour may the earth be constantly rich in grain.
May there be auspiciousness without obstacles; may plagues be completely pacified!

2.32.s:
namaste devadeveśa namaste balasūdana ..
namucighna namaste'stu sahasrākṣa śacīpate .. 15 ..
2.32.d:
नमस्ते देवदेवेश नमस्ते बलसूदन ॥
नमुचिघ्न नमस्तेऽस्तु सहस्राक्ष शचीपते ॥ 15 ॥
2.32.m:
Homage to you, O lord of the god of gods! Homage to you, O slayer of Bala!
O slayer of Namuci, homage be to you, O thousand-eyed one, O husband of Śacī!

2.32.s:
sarveṣāmeva lokānāṃ tvamekā paramā gatiḥ ..
tvameva paramaḥ prāṇaḥ sarvasyāsya jagatpate .. 16 ..
2.32.d:
सर्वेषामेव लोकानां त्वमेका परमा गतिः ॥
त्वमेव परमः प्राणः सर्वस्यास्य जगत्पते ॥ 16 ॥
2.32.m:
You alone are the supreme refuge of all worlds;
you alone are the supreme breath of life of all this [universe], O lord of the world!

2.32.s:
pāśo hyasi pathaḥ sraṣṭuṃ tvamanalpaṃ purandara ..
tvameva meghastvaṃ vāyustvamagnirvaidyutombare .. 17..
2.32.d:
पाशो ह्यसि पथः स्रष्टुं त्वमनल्पं पुरन्दर ॥
त्वमेव मेघस्त्वं वायुस्त्वमग्निर्वैद्युतोम्बरे ॥ 17॥
2.32.m:
You are indeed the noose to create a boundless path, O Purandara;
you alone are the cloud, you are the wind, you are the lightning-fire in the sky.

2.32.s:
tvamatra medhā vikṣiptā tvamme bāhuḥ pratardanam..
tvaṃ vajramatulaṃ ghoraṃ ghoṣavāṃstvaṃ balāhakaḥ .. 18 ..
2.32.d:
त्वमत्र मेधा विक्षिप्ता त्वम्मे बाहुः प्रतर्दनम्॥
त्वं वज्रमतुलं घोरं घोषवांस्त्वं बलाहकः ॥ 18 ॥
2.32.m:
You are intelligence projected here; you are my arm, the destroyer;
you are the incomparable, terrible thunderbolt; you are the rumbling cloud.

2.32.s:
sraṣṭā tvameva lokānāṃ saṃhartā cāparājitaḥ ..
tvaṃ jyotiḥ sarvalokānāṃ tvamādityo vibhāvasuḥ..19..
2.32.d:
स्रष्टा त्वमेव लोकानां संहर्ता चापराजितः ॥
त्वं ज्योतिः सर्वलोकानां त्वमादित्यो विभावसुः॥19॥
2.32.m:
You alone are the creator of the worlds, and the undefeated destroyer;
you are the light of all worlds; you are the Sun, the fire.

2.32.s:
tvaṃ mahadbhūtamāścaryaṃ tvaṃ rājā tvaṃ surottamaḥ ..
tvaṃ viṣṇustvaṃ sahasrākṣastvaṃ devastvaṃ parāyaṇam... .. 2.157.20..
2.32.d:
त्वं महद्भूतमाश्चर्यं त्वं राजा त्वं सुरोत्तमः ॥
त्वं विष्णुस्त्वं सहस्राक्षस्त्वं देवस्त्वं परायणम्॥॥। 2.157.20॥
2.32.m:
You are the great wonder of existence; you are the king; you are the highest of gods;
you are Viṣṇu; you are the thousand-eyed one; you are the god; you are the final resort.

2.32.s:
tvameva cāmṛtaṃ devastvaṃ mokṣaḥ paramārcitaḥ ..
tvaṃ muhūrtaḥ sthitistvaṃ ca lavastvaṃ ca punaḥ kṣaṇaḥ ..21..
2.32.d:
त्वमेव चामृतं देवस्त्वं मोक्षः परमार्चितः ॥
त्वं मुहूर्तः स्थितिस्त्वं च लवस्त्वं च पुनः क्षणः ॥21॥
2.32.m:
You alone are the nectar, the god; you are liberation, supremely worshipped;
you are the muhūrta, the duration, the lava, and again the kṣaṇa;

2.32.s:
śuklastvaṃ bahulaścaiva kalā kāṣṭhā truṭistathā ..
saṃvatsarartavo māsā rajanyaśca dināni ca ..22..
2.32.d:
शुक्लस्त्वं बहुलश्चैव कला काष्ठा त्रुटिस्तथा ॥
संवत्सरर्तवो मासा रजन्यश्च दिनानि च ॥22॥
2.32.m:
you are the light [fortnight] and the dark [fortnight], the kalā, the kāṣṭhā, and the truṭi;
the years, the seasons, the months, the nights, and the days.

2.32.s:
tvamuttamā sagiricarā vasuṃdharā sabhāskaraṃ timiramambaraṃ tathā ..
sahodadhiḥ satimiṅgilastathā sahormivānbahumakaro jhaṣākulaḥ ..23..
2.32.d:
त्वमुत्तमा सगिरिचरा वसुंधरा सभास्करं तिमिरमम्बरं तथा ॥
सहोदधिः सतिमिङ्गिलस्तथा सहोर्मिवान्बहुमकरो झषाकुलः ॥23॥

2.32.s:
mahadyaśāstvamiha sadā ca pūjyase maharṣibhirmuditamanā maharṣibhiḥ ..
abhiṣṭutaḥ pibasi ca somamadhvare hutānyapi ca havīṃṣi bhūtaye .. 24 ..
2.32.d:
महद्यशास्त्वमिह सदा च पूज्यसे महर्षिभिर्मुदितमना महर्षिभिः ॥
अभिष्टुतः पिबसि च सोममध्वरे हुतान्यपि च हवींषि भूतये ॥ 24 ॥
2.32.m:
You of great renown are always worshipped here by the great sages with delighted minds;
praised by the great sages, you drink the soma at the sacrifice and [accept] the oblations offered for prosperity.

2.32.s:
tvaṃ vipraiḥ satatamihejyase phalārthaṃ bhedārtheṣvaṣṭasu balaugha gīyase tvam ..
tvaddhetoryajanapārāyaṇā dvijendrā vedāṅgānyadhigamayanti sarvavedaiḥ .. 25 ..
2.32.d:
त्वं विप्रैः सततमिहेज्यसे फलार्थं भेदार्थेष्वष्टसु बलौघ गीयसे त्वम् ॥
त्वद्धेतोर्यजनपारायणा द्विजेन्द्रा वेदाङ्गान्यधिगमयन्ति सर्ववेदैः ॥ 25 ॥

2.32.s:
vajrasya bhartā bhuvanasya goptā vṛtrasya hartā namucernihantā ..
kṛṣṇe vasāno vasane mahātmā satyānṛte yo vivinakti loke ..26..
2.32.d:
वज्रस्य भर्ता भुवनस्य गोप्ता वृत्रस्य हर्ता नमुचेर्निहन्ता ॥
कृष्णे वसानो वसने महात्मा सत्यानृते यो विविनक्ति लोके ॥26॥
2.32.m:
Wielder of the thunderbolt, guardian of the world, slayer of Vṛtra, destroyer of Namuci;
the great-souled one clad in dark garments, who distinguishes truth and falsehood in the world.

2.32.s:
yaṃ vājinaṃ garbhamapāṃ surāṇāṃ vaiśvānaraṃ vāhanamabhyupaiti ..
namaḥ sadā'smai tridiveśvarāya lokatrayeśāya purandarāya .. 27 ...
2.32.d:
यं वाजिनं गर्भमपां सुराणां वैश्वानरं वाहनमभ्युपैति ॥
नमः सदाऽस्मै त्रिदिवेश्वराय लोकत्रयेशाय पुरन्दराय ॥ 27 ॥।
2.32.m:
He whose steed is Vaiśvānara, the womb of the waters of the gods, who approaches as his mount—
homage always to this ruler of heaven, the lord of the three worlds, Purandara!

2.32.s:
ajo'vyayaḥ śāśvata ekarūpo viṣṇurvarāhaḥ puruṣaḥ purāṇaḥ ..
tvamantakaḥ sarvaharaḥ kṛśānuḥ saharṣaśīrṣā śatamanyurīḍyaḥ .. 28 ..
2.32.d:
अजोऽव्ययः शाश्वत एकरूपो विष्णुर्वराहः पुरुषः पुराणः ॥
त्वमन्तकः सर्वहरः कृशानुः सहर्षशीर्षा शतमन्युरीड्यः ॥ 28 ॥
2.32.m:
Unborn, imperishable, eternal, of single form, Viṣṇu, the Boar, the ancient Cosmic Person,
you are the ender, taking away all, fire, having a thousand heads, Śatamanyu, worthy of praise.

2.32.s:
kaviṃ saptajihvaṃ trātāramindraṃ savitāraṃ sureśam ..
hṛdayābhiśakraṃ vṛtrahaṇaṃ suṣeṇamasmākaṃ vīrā uttare bhavantu .. 29 ..
2.32.d:
कविं सप्तजिह्वं त्रातारमिन्द्रं सवितारं सुरेशम् ॥
हृदयाभिशक्रं वृत्रहणं सुषेणमस्माकं वीरा उत्तरे भवन्तु ॥ 29 ॥
2.32.m:
The sage, seven-tongued, Indra the protector, Savitṛ, the lord of gods,
Śakra who gladdens the heart, slayer of Vṛtra, having good armies: may our heroes be superior!

2.32.s:
trātāramindrendriyakāraṇātmañjagatpradhānaṃ ca hiraṇyagarbham ..
lokeśvaraṃ devavaraṃ vareṇyaṃ cānandarūpaṃ praṇatosmi nityama .. 2.157.30 ..
2.32.d:
त्रातारमिन्द्रेन्द्रियकारणात्मञ्जगत्प्रधानं च हिरण्यगर्भम् ॥
लोकेश्वरं देववरं वरेण्यं चानन्दरूपं प्रणतोस्मि नित्यम ॥ 2.157.30 ॥
2.32.m:
To Indra the protector, the self that is the cause of the senses, the foremost principle of the universe, Hiraṇyagarbha,
the lord of the world, the best of gods, worthy of choice, whose form is bliss—to him I bow perpetually."

2.32.s:
imaṃ stavaṃ devavarasya kīrtayenmahātmanastridaśapateḥ susaṃyataḥ ..
avāpya kāmānmanasobhirāmānsvarlokamāyāti ca dehabhede .. 31 ..
2.158
rāma uvāca ..
vidhinā pūjayetkena bhadrakālīṃ narādhipaḥ ..
navamyāmāśvine māsi śuklapakṣe narottama.. 1 ..
puṣkara uvāca ..
pūrvottare tu digbhāge śibirātsumanohare ..
bhadrakālīgṛhaṃ kuryāccitravastrairalaṃkṛtam .. 2..
bhadrakālīṃ paṭe kṛtvā tatra sampūjayeddvija..
āśvine śuklapakṣe tu aṣṭamyāṃ prayatastataḥ..3..
tatraivāyudhavarmādyaṃ chatraṃ ketuṃ ca pūjayet ..
rājaliṅgāni sarvāṇi tathāstrāṇi ca pūjayeta ..4..
puṣpairgandhaiḥ phalairbhakṣyerbhojyaiśca sumanoharaiḥ ..
bahubhiśca vicitrābhiḥ prekṣādānaistathaiva ca..5..
rātrau jāgaraṇaṃ kuryāttatraiva vasudhādhipaḥ ..
evaṃ saṃpūjayeddevīṃ varadāṃ bhaktavatsalām..6..
2.32.d:
इमं स्तवं देववरस्य कीर्तयेन्महात्मनस्त्रिदशपतेः सुसंयतः ॥
अवाप्य कामान्मनसोभिरामान्स्वर्लोकमायाति च देहभेदे ॥ 31 ॥
2.158
राम उवाच ॥
विधिना पूजयेत्केन भद्रकालीं नराधिपः ॥
नवम्यामाश्विने मासि शुक्लपक्षे नरोत्तम॥ 1 ॥
पुष्कर उवाच ॥
पूर्वोत्तरे तु दिग्भागे शिबिरात्सुमनोहरे ॥
भद्रकालीगृहं कुर्याच्चित्रवस्त्रैरलंकृतम् ॥ 2॥
भद्रकालीं पटे कृत्वा तत्र सम्पूजयेद्द्विज॥
आश्विने शुक्लपक्षे तु अष्टम्यां प्रयतस्ततः॥3॥
तत्रैवायुधवर्माद्यं छत्रं केतुं च पूजयेत् ॥
राजलिङ्गानि सर्वाणि तथास्त्राणि च पूजयेत ॥4॥
पुष्पैर्गन्धैः फलैर्भक्ष्येर्भोज्यैश्च सुमनोहरैः ॥
बहुभिश्च विचित्राभिः प्रेक्षादानैस्तथैव च॥5॥
रात्रौ जागरणं कुर्यात्तत्रैव वसुधाधिपः ॥
एवं संपूजयेद्देवीं वरदां भक्तवत्सलाम्॥6॥
2.32.m:
One who, thoroughly self-restrained, recites this praise of the best of gods, the great-souled lord of the thirty [gods],
obtaining the desires pleasing to his mind, goes to the world of heaven upon the dissolution of the body.
2.158
Rāma said:
By what procedure should a ruler of men worship Bhadrakālī
on the ninth lunar day of the light fortnight in the month of Āśvina, O best of men?
Puṣkara said:
In the north-eastern direction from the military camp, in a very pleasant spot,
he should construct a house for Bhadrakālī, adorned with multicoloured cloth.
Having depicted Bhadrakālī on a cloth, the twice-born should worship her there,
with self-restraint, on the eighth lunar day in the light fortnight of Āśvina.
Right there he should worship the weapons, armour, parasol, and banner;
he should worship all the royal insignia as well as the missile weapons,
with flowers, perfumes, fruits, snacks, and most delightful foods,
and with many diverse theatrical presentations and gifts.
The ruler of the earth should keep vigil there throughout the night;
thus he should worship the goddess who grants boons and is affectionate to her devotees,

2.32.s:
kātyāyanīṃ kāmagamāṃ vararūpāṃ varapradām..
pūjitāṃ sarvakāmaiśca sā yuṅkte vasudhādhipam ..7..
evaṃ hi sampūjya jagatpradhānaṃ yātrā tu deyā vasudhādhipena ..
prāpnoti siddhiṃ paramāṃ maheśo janastathānyo'pi hi vittaśaktyā .. 8 ..
2.159
rāma uvāca ..
nīrājanavidhiṃ tvattaḥ śrotumicchāmi sattama ..
kathaṃ kāryā narendrasya śāntiṃ nīrājane prabho .. 1 ..
puṣkara uvāca ..
pūrvottare tu digbhāge nagarātsumanohare ..
vistīrṇaṃ kārayedrājā manoharamāśrayam .. 2 ..
kaṭairguptaṃ kuśāstīrṇaṃ patākādhvajaśobhitam ..
toraṇatritayaṃ tatra prāṅmukhaṃ kārayecchubham .. 3 ..
kāryaṃ ṣoḍaśahastaṃ tu toraṇaṃ tu samucchritam ..
vaipulyaṃ daśahastaṃ tu tatra kāryaṃ bhṛgūttama .. 4 ..
toraṇāddakṣiṇe bhāge tatra kāryaṃ samāśrayam ..
devatārcā bhavedyatra tathāgnihavana kriyā .. 5 ..
2.32.d:
कात्यायनीं कामगमां वररूपां वरप्रदाम्॥
पूजितां सर्वकामैश्च सा युङ्क्ते वसुधाधिपम् ॥7॥
एवं हि सम्पूज्य जगत्प्रधानं यात्रा तु देया वसुधाधिपेन ॥
प्राप्नोति सिद्धिं परमां महेशो जनस्तथान्योऽपि हि वित्तशक्त्या ॥ 8 ॥
2.159
राम उवाच ॥
नीराजनविधिं त्वत्तः श्रोतुमिच्छामि सत्तम ॥
कथं कार्या नरेन्द्रस्य शान्तिं नीराजने प्रभो ॥ 1 ॥
पुष्कर उवाच ॥
पूर्वोत्तरे तु दिग्भागे नगरात्सुमनोहरे ॥
विस्तीर्णं कारयेद्राजा मनोहरमाश्रयम् ॥ 2 ॥
कटैर्गुप्तं कुशास्तीर्णं पताकाध्वजशोभितम् ॥
तोरणत्रितयं तत्र प्राङ्मुखं कारयेच्छुभम् ॥ 3 ॥
कार्यं षोडशहस्तं तु तोरणं तु समुच्छ्रितम् ॥
वैपुल्यं दशहस्तं तु तत्र कार्यं भृगूत्तम ॥ 4 ॥
तोरणाद्दक्षिणे भागे तत्र कार्यं समाश्रयम् ॥
देवतार्चा भवेद्यत्र तथाग्निहवन क्रिया ॥ 5 ॥
2.32.m:
Kātyāyanī, who moves at will, of excellent form, who grants boons;
when worshipped, she endows the ruler of the earth with all desires.
Having thus worshipped the foremost [power] of the universe, a military march should be undertaken by the ruler of the earth;
the great lord attains supreme success, and any other person also does so according to his financial capacity.
2.159
Rāma said:
O best of virtuous beings, I wish to hear from you the rule of the lustration rite. / How should the pacification rite in the lustration be performed for a king, O lord?
Puṣkara said:
In the north-eastern direction from the city, in a very pleasant place, / the king should have a spacious and delightful shelter erected.
Enclosed with mats, strewn with kuśa grass, adorned with pennants and banners, / he should have three auspicious archways erected there, facing eastward.
An archway should be made sixteen cubits high, / and its breadth should be made ten cubits, O foremost of the Bhṛgus.
To the south of the archway, he should make an enclosure / where the worship of deities and the offering into the fire may take place.

2.32.m:
To the left, an eight-cubit long and high / heap of dry brand-sticks is to be erected, O scion of Bhṛgu’s lineage.
With five-coloured thread he should make a charming [cord] with a hundred knots, / a hundred-loop snare positioned in the middle, at the middle archway.
Having covered it with kuśa grass, he should then cover it with clay. / It must be zealously avoided from being stepped over by any creature,
so long as it has not first been crossed over by the royal elephant. / When the sun departs from Citrā and enters Svātī,
from then on it must be performed, as long as the sun remains in Svātī; / each day in the enclosure the deities must be worshipped, O best of the twice-born:
Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śambhu, Śakra, Fire and Wind, / Vināyaka, Kumāra, Varuṇa, Dhanada, Yama,
the Viśvedevas, O fortunate one, and Uccaiḥśravas. / The eight great elephants are to be worshipped; hear their names from me:

हुत्वा च कलशान्कुर्यात्सोदकान्गन्धसंयुतान् ॥

2.32.m:
Kumuda, Airāvaṇa, Padma, Puṣpadanta, then Vāmana, / Supratīka, Añjana, and Nīla; these eight are of divine origin.
The worship of the planets and lunar mansions must likewise be performed by the royal priest. / Then, with focused mind, the priest should offer oblations into the fire,
for the desired deities with the mantras that bear their designations, / and for those lacking mantras, with the Praṇava, O mighty-armed one.
Fuel sticks of milky trees, and white mustard seeds, / ghee, sesame seeds, O knower of dharma, and unbroken grains of rice,
having offered these, he should set up jars containing water and fragrant substances, / worshipped with garlands and perfumes, and adorned with shoots of trees,
and wrap them in cloth with five-coloured cord. / Marking-nut, rice, white mustard, sweet flag, costus, and priyaṅgu—
to the west of the archway, with the previously prepared jars, / the best elephants should then be bathed [by priests] sanctified with mantras,

तुरगांश्च महाभाग चालङ्कृत्य ततस्तु तान् ॥
ततोभिषेकनागस्य तथा तत्तुरगस्य च ॥2.159.20॥
अन्नपिण्डं ततो देयमभिमन्त्र्य पुरोधसा ॥
तस्याभिनन्दने राज्ञो विनयः परिकीर्तितः ॥ 21 ॥
त्यागे च तस्य विज्ञेयं महद्भयमुपस्थितम् ॥
निष्क्रामयेत्तोरणैस्तु ततो हि प्रथमं गजान् ॥ 22 ॥
तत्रापि प्रथमं राम अभिषिच्य गजोत्तमम् ॥
तस्यादौ शतपाशीं तु नरः पञ्चनखोऽपि वा ॥ 23 ॥
अथ ह्यन्यो लंघयेत्तां राज्ञो मरणमादिशेत् ॥
दुर्भिक्षं तत्र विज्ञेयं गोखरोष्ट्रैश्च लंघने ॥ 24 ॥
लंघयेद्वामपादेन यदि तां नृपकुञ्जरः ॥
राजा पुरोहितामात्यराजपुत्रहितं भवेत् ॥25 ॥
राज्ञस्तु मरणं बूयादाक्रमेत्तं यदापरः ॥
राज्ञोपि जयमाचष्टे लंघयेन्दक्षिणेन ताम् ॥ 26 ॥
2.32.m:
and the horses, O fortunate one; and then, having adorned them, / next, for the consecrated elephant and that consecrated horse,
a ball of food should then be given by the royal priest after consecrating it with mantras. / In its acceptance [of the food], the king's discipline and success are proclaimed;
in its rejection, it is to be known that a great danger has approached. / Then he should cause the elephants to go out first through the archways.
There too, first, O Rāma, having sprinkled the best of elephants— / if before it a human, or a five-clawed animal,
or any other should step over that hundred-loop cord, one should predict the king's death. / If it is crossed by cows, donkeys, or camels, famine is to be understood there.
If the royal elephant should step over it with its left foot, / it brings welfare to the king, the royal priest, the ministers, and the prince.
One should declare death for the king if another [foot] should tread upon it; / if it crosses it with the right foot, it announces victory for the king.

2.32.m: and with the leaps of the delighted infantry, O best of men, / having done thus, the king should go home, preceded by his army.

2.32.m: And having honoured the people, he should dismiss everyone from his palace. / This pacification rite named Nīrājanā should be performed by rulers of the earth; / it brings security and fosters growth, O Rāma, for men, elephants, and horses.

तथा दुन्दुभिचापानां ब्रूहि मन्त्रान्ममानघ ॥ 1 ॥

शृणु मन्त्रान्महाभाग भगवान्यत्पराशरः ॥
गालवाय पुरोवाच सर्वधर्मभृतां वरः ॥ 2 ॥
पराशर उवाच ॥
यथाम्बुदश्छादयति शिवायेमां वसुन्धराम ॥
तथाच्छादय राजानं विजयारोग्यवृद्धये ॥ 3 ॥
इति च्छत्रमन्त्रः ॥
पराशर उवाच ॥
गन्धर्वकुलराजस्त्वं मा भूयाः कुलदूषकः ॥
ब्रह्मणः सत्यवाक्येन सोमस्य वरुणस्य च ॥ 4 ॥
प्रभावश्च हुताशस्य भवस्य त्वं तुरङ्गम ॥
तेजसा चैव सूर्यस्य मुनीनां तपसां तथा ॥ 5 ॥
2.32.m:
It brings fortune, bestows fame, destroys enemies, conveys happiness, and is the highest pacification rite. / It should be performed by kings for the prospering of their realm with every effort, O hero of the Bhṛgus.

Rāma said: / Tell me, O sinless one, the mantras for the umbrella, the flag, the elephants, / the banner, the sword, and the armour, as well as for the kettle-drums and bows.
Puṣkara said: / Hear, O fortunate one, the mantras that the venerable Parāśara, / the foremost of all upholders of dharma, formerly spoke to Gālava.
Parāśara said: / Just as a raincloud covers this earth for its welfare, / so cover the king for the increase of victory and health.
Thus ends the mantra for the umbrella.
Parāśara said: / You are a king of the Gandharva lineage; do not become a defiler of your race! / By the truthful word of Brahmā, and of Soma and Varuṇa,
and by the power of the Fire-eater and of Bhava, O horse, / and by the radiance of Sūrya, and likewise the austerities of the sages,

2.32.d:
रुद्रस्य ब्रह्मचर्येण पवनस्य बलेन च ॥
स्मर त्वं राजपुत्रोऽसि कौस्तुभं च मणिं स्मर ॥6॥
यां गतिं ब्रह्महा गच्छेत्पितृहा मातृहा तथा ॥
भूम्यर्थेऽनृतवादी च क्षत्त्रियश्च पराङ्मुखः ॥ 7 ॥
सूर्याचन्द्रमसौ वायुर्यावत्पश्यन्ति दुष्कृतम् ॥
व्रजेत्त्वेतां गतिं क्षिप्रं तच्च पापं भवेत्तव ॥ 8 ॥
विकृतिं यदि गच्छेन्नो युद्धेऽध्वनि तुरङ्गम ॥
रिपून्विजित्य समरे सहभर्त्रा सुखी भव ॥ 9 ॥
इत्यश्वमन्त्रः ॥
पराशर उवाच ॥
शक्रकेतो महावीर सुपर्णस्तत्सुताश्रितः ॥
पतत्रिराट् वैनतेयस्तथा नारायणध्वजः ॥ 2.160.10 ॥
काश्यपेयोऽमृताहर्ता नागारिर्विष्णुवाहनः ॥
अप्रमेयो दुराधर्षो रणे चैवारिसूदनः ॥ 11 ॥ ।
गरुत्मान्मारुतगतिः त्वयि सन्निहितः स्थितः ॥
साश्ववर्मायुधान्योधान्रक्षास्माकं महद्रिपून् ॥ 12॥
2.32.m:
by the chastity of Rudra and the strength of the Wind: / remember that you are a prince, and remember the Kaustubha jewel!
Whatever fate a slayer of a brahmin would meet, or a slayer of a father or mother, / or one who speaks falsely regarding land, or a kṣatriya who turns his back [in flight],
for as long as the sun, moon, and wind behold evil deeds— / to that fate may you swiftly go, and may that sin be yours,
if you should fail us in battle or on the march, O horse! / Having conquered the enemies in battle, be happy along with your master.
Thus ends the mantra for the horse.
Parāśara said: / O great hero, standard of Śakra, fair-winged bird resting on his son, / king of birds, Vainateya, and emblem of Nārāyaṇa,
son of Kaśyapa, bringer of the nectar, enemy of serpents, mount of Viṣṇu, / immeasurable, invincible, and slayer of foes in battle,
Garutmān, possessing the swiftness of the wind, abiding present within you: / protect our warriors along with their horses, armour, and weapons, [and destroy] the great foes!

कुमुदैरावणौ पद्मः पुष्पदन्तोथ वामनः ॥
सुप्रतीकोञ्जनो नील एतेष्टौ देवयोनयः ॥ 13 ॥
तेषां पुत्राश्च पौत्राश्च धनान्यष्टौ समाश्रिताः ॥
भद्रो मन्दो मृगश्चैव गजः संकीर्ण एव च ॥ 14 ॥
वनेवने प्रसृतास्ते स्मर योनिं महागज ॥
पान्तु त्वां वसवो रुद्रा आदित्याः समरुद्गणाः ॥ 15 ॥
भर्तारं रक्ष नागेन्द्र समयः प्रतिपाल्यताम् ॥
अवाप्नुहि जयं युद्धे गमने स्वस्ति नो व्रज ॥ 16 ॥
श्रीस्ते सोमाद्बलं विष्णोस्तेजः सूर्याज्जवोऽनिलात् ॥
स्थैर्यं मेरोर्जयं रुद्राद्यशो देवात्पुरन्दरात् ॥ 17 ॥
युद्धे रक्षन्तु नागास्त्वां दिशश्च सह दैवतैः ॥
अश्विभ्यां सह गन्धर्वा पान्तु त्वां सर्वतः सदा ॥ 18 ॥
इति हस्तिमंत्रः ॥
पराशर उवाच ॥
हुतभुग्वसवो रुद्रा वायुः सोमो महर्षयः ॥
नागकिन्नरगन्धर्वयज्ञभूतगणग्रहाः ॥ 19 ॥
2.32.m:
Thus ends the mantra for the standard.
Parāśara said: / Kumuda, Airāvaṇa, Padma, Puṣpadanta, then Vāmana, / Supratīka, Añjana, and Nīla—these eight are of divine origin.
Their sons and grandsons resorted to the eight quarters: / the bhadra, the manda, the mṛga, and the saṃkīrṇa elephant.
They have spread through every forest; remember your lineage, O great elephant! / May the Vasus, the Rudras, and the Ādityas along with the troops of Maruts protect you.
Protect your master, O lord of elephants; let the pact be observed! / Attain victory in battle, and march on our journey with blessing!
May your splendour be from Soma, your strength from Viṣṇu, your radiance from Sūrya, your speed from the Wind, / your steadfastness from Meru, your victory from Rudra, and your fame from the divine Purandara.
In battle, may the elephants of the directions along with their deities protect you; / may the Gandharvas along with the two Aśvins guard you on all sides at all times.
Thus ends the mantra for the elephant.
Parāśara said: / The Fire-eater, the Vasus, the Rudras, the Wind, Soma, the great sages, / Nāgas, Kinnaras, Gandharvas, the hosts of sacrifice, spirits, and planets,

2.32.d:
प्रमथास्तु सहादित्यैर्भूतेशो मातृभिः सहः ॥
शक्रसेनापतिः स्कन्दो वरुणश्चाश्रितस्त्वयि ॥ 2.160.20 ॥
प्रदहन्तु रिपून्सर्वान्राजा विजयमिच्छतु ॥
यानि प्रयुक्तान्यरिभिर्दूषणानि समन्ततः ॥ 21 ॥
पतन्तूपरि शत्रूणां हतानि तव तेजसा ॥
कालनेमिवधे यद्वद्यश्च त्रिपुरपातने ॥ 22 ॥
हिरण्यकशिपोर्यद्वद्वधे सर्वासुरेषु च ॥
शोभितासि तथैवाद्य शोभस्व समयं स्मर ॥ 23 ॥
नीलाञ्श्वेतानिमान्दृष्ट्वा नश्यंत्वाशु नृपारयः ॥
व्याधिभिर्विविधैर्घोरैः शस्त्रैश्च युधि निर्जिताः ॥ 24 ॥
पूतना रेवती नाम्ना कालरात्रीति पठ्यते ॥
दहत्वाशु रिपून्सर्वान्पताके त्वामुपाश्रिता ॥ 25 ॥
इति पताकामन्त्रः ॥
पराशर उवाच ॥
असिर्विशसनः खड्गस्तीक्ष्णधारो दुरासदः ॥
श्रीगर्भो विजयश्चैव धर्माचारस्तथैव च ॥ 26 ॥
2.32.m:
the Pramathas along with the Ādityas, the Lord of Spirits with the Mothers, / Skanda the general of Śakra's army, and Varuṇa have taken their abode in you.
May they burn all the enemies; let the king desire victory! / Whatever bewitchments have been employed by the foes on every side,
let them fall upon the enemies, destroyed by your splendour! / Just as in the slaying of Kālanemi, and that which was in the overthrow of Tripura,
and just as in the slaying of Hiraṇyakaśipu and among all the asuras, / you were radiant, so shine today; remember your pledge!
Beholding these blue and white [banners], let the king's enemies swiftly perish, / overcome in battle by various dreadful afflictions and by weapons.
She who is recited as Pūtanā, by name Revatī, and Kālarātrī, / resting upon you, O banner, let her swiftly burn all the enemies!
Thus ends the mantra for the banner.
Parāśara said: / Sword, Slaughterer, Scimitar, Sharp-edged, Difficult to Approach, / Womb of Fortune, Victory, and Conduct of Dharma—

2.32.d:
इत्यष्टौ तव नामानि स्वयमुक्तानि वेधसा ॥
नक्षत्रं कृत्तिका तुभ्यं गुरुर्देवो महेश्वरः ॥ 27 ॥
रोहिण्याश्च शरीरं ते दैवतं तु जनार्दनः ॥
पिता पितामहो देवः स त्वं पालय सर्वदा ॥ 28 ॥
इति खड्गमन्त्रः ॥
पराशर उवाच ॥
वर्मप्रदस्त्वं समरे धर्मसैन्याय मानद ॥
रक्ष मां रक्षणीयोऽहं तवानघ नमोस्तु ते ॥ 29 ॥
इति वर्ममन्त्रः ॥
पराशर उवाच ॥
दुन्दुभे त्वं सपत्नानां घोषाद्धृदयकंपनः ॥ 2.160.30 ॥
तव भूमिपसैन्यानां तथा विजयवर्धनः ॥
यथा जीमूतघोषेण हृष्यन्ति शरवारणाः ॥
तथा च तव शब्देन त्रस्यन्त्वस्मद्द्विषो रणे ॥ 31 ॥
इति दुन्दुभिमंत्रः ॥
पराशर उवाच ॥
सर्वायुधमहामात्र सर्वदेवारिसूदन ॥
चापस्त्वं सर्वदा रक्ष साकं शरवरैः सदा ॥ 32 ॥
2.32.m:
these are your eight names, spoken by the Creator himself. / The constellation Kṛttikā is yours; your preceptor is the god Maheśvara;
your body is of Rohiṇī, and your deity is Janārdana. / Your father and grandfather is God; so do you protect at all times.
Thus ends the mantra for the sword.
Parāśara said: / You bestow armour in battle upon the army of dharma, O honour-giver; / protect me, for I am to be protected by you, O sinless one; homage be to you!
Thus ends the mantra for the armour.
Parāśara said: / O kettle-drum, you make the hearts of adversaries tremble with your sound,
and likewise increase the victory of your king's armies! / Just as cloud-dispelling elephants rejoice at the rumble of a raincloud, / so let our enemies tremble in battle at your sound!
Thus ends the mantra for the kettle-drum.
Parāśara said: / O supreme among all weapons, O slayer of all the enemies of the gods, / you are the bow; protect always, together with excellent arrows at all times!

etaistu maṃtrairabhimantritānāṃ calatyamoghaṃ balamapramṛṣyam .. 33 ..
2.32.d:
इति चापमन्त्रः ॥
पुष्कर उवाच ॥
मंत्रास्तवैतेऽभिहिता नृवीर सम्मंत्रणे वैजयिका यथावत् ॥
एतैस्तु मंत्रैरभिमन्त्रितानां चलत्यमोघं बलमप्रमृष्यम् ॥ 33 ॥
2.32.m:
Thus ends the mantra for the bow.
Puṣkara said: / These mantras, bringing victory when consecration is duly made, have been told to you, O hero among men; / consecrated with these mantras, an irresistible and unfailing force advances.
